summary: XRD analysis across all quantum dot (QD) films with different ligands (PEABr, ThEABr, ThPABr, ThBABr) reveals identical peak positions corresponding to the CsPbBr3 cubic phase, indicating that ligand substitution does not alter the primary crystal structure. No evidence of secondary phases or significant structural changes is observed. However, quantitative details such as peak intensity, FWHM, or lattice parameters are not provided, limiting assessment of crystallinity or subtle structural effects.

key_findings.finding: All QD films (PEABr, ThEABr, ThPABr, ThBABr) exhibit three main XRD peaks at 15°, 21°, and 31°, corresponding to the (100), (110), and (200) planes of the CsPbBr3 cubic phase.
Peak positions are consistent across all ligand-modified QD films, with no detectable shift or emergence of new peaks.

scientific_interpretation.claim: The primary crystal structure of CsPbBr3 QDs remains cubic and unchanged by substitution of PEABr with ThEABr, ThPABr, or ThBABr ligands.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: All samples show identical peak positions at 15°, 21°, and 31°, with no new peaks or shifts, indicating structural retention across ligand types.

citations.evidence: All samples show three main peaks at 15°, 21°, and 31°

scientific_interpretation.claim: There is no evidence for the formation of secondary phases or significant structural transformation upon ligand exchange in these QD films.
scientific_interpretation.reasoning: No additional peaks or phase assignments are reported for any ligand condition, suggesting phase purity is maintained.

citations.evidence: three distinct diffraction peaks are observed at 15°, 21°, and 31°, corresponding to the (100), (110), and (200) crystal planes of the CsPbBr3 cubic phase, respectively

limitations.claim: No quantitative information on peak intensity or FWHM is provided, preventing assessment of crystallinity, grain size, or subtle structural changes.
Lattice parameters are not reported, so potential minor lattice distortions or strain effects due to ligand substitution cannot be evaluated.
Only one XRD figure is present, limiting the ability to assess reproducibility or trends under other experimental variables.
